studies.title: BLM18AG601SN1 · FB120, FB130
studies.summary: Exact manufacturer frequency-dependent bead model executed in ngspice. Quantifies the part in an assumed reference fixture.
assumptions: 50 Ω source and load are characterization-fixture assumptions; they are not extracted PCB or IC impedances.
Excitation is a 10 mV peak perturbation at zero DC bias; no operating rail voltage or load current is superimposed.
The individual model header specifies 25 °C. The library webpage has a generic 20 °C remark; the per-file condition is used.
limitations: Applicable only from 1 MHz to 3 GHz, small signal, zero DC bias. No saturation, current derating or temperature dependence.
Model RLC coefficients fit RF terminal behavior; extrapolated DC resistance is not a part rating. BLM21PG601SN1 fit gives 0.17 Ω at DC while the retained catalog maximum is 0.14 Ω.
No board return path, cable, biased MLCC, EMI receiver or radiation model. Fixture insertion response is not board attenuation or EMC compliance.
First-cycle turn-on is outside the reported settled-sine assessment; startup settling includes frequencies outside the fitted band.

studies.title: RESETn · actual RC network, assumed control
studies.summary: Separate analog SPICE experiment includes both physical reset capacitors and pull-up, which the older digital reset diagram omits.
assumptions: 3.3 V pull-up rail ramps in 1 ms and is stable before the assumed 40 ms open-drain release.
PMIC output is a substitute switch: 10 Ω asserted, 1 TΩ released. This is not an RK809-5 macro or OTP sequence.
70% of 3.3 V is an illustrative receiver threshold, not a newly qualified RK3566 reset specification.
Effective capacitance factors 1.0, 0.7 and 0.4 and optional 10 µA leakage are sensitivities, not measured part corners.
limitations: No PMIC default timing, SoC activity or firmware executes. Real sink current, leakage, allowable edge rate and thresholds remain to qualify.
No board temperature or boot-pass conclusion. This study does not rewrite the saved 40 ms requested-reset window.

studies.title: ISSI DDR3L input models on four native DM routes
studies.summary: 25 ngspice receive-channel cases use exact-family ISSI nonlinear input/ODT and pin RLC data. Rockchip drive and uniform channel parameters are explicit sensitivity assumptions.
studies.model_type: Vendor IBIS input subset + native route geometry + assumed source/channel

sources.title: ISSI DDR3 product table: IS43TR16512BL 1.35 V model link
IBIS 4.2 specification, input/clamp and package conventions
ngspice 42 manual, behavioral PWL and lossless transmission lines

assumptions: Exact ISSI 43tr16512bl component, DM_ODT0/40/60/120 input models, per-pin D3/E7 package RLC; speed-bin and lot correlation are not supplied in the model.
Assumed U1 source at its PCB ball: ideal 0–VDD PWL pulse plus 20/34/60 ohm source resistance. No exact Rockchip I/O or package model; these are sensitivity values, not decoded register settings.
Isolated pulse only: rise starts 1 ns, full 0–100% edge 100/250/500 ps, fall starts 3.5 ns, finish 7 ns. This is not a DDR command/data transaction or 1600 MT/s eye test.
Supplies and the selected ODT state are already present in the DC operating point before t=0. A terminated low input can therefore sit above ground; this time axis is not power-up or boot time.

Measured route length includes planar copper plus via-axis distance using the saved proposed stack. It drives one uniform lossless line, assumed 40/50/60 ohm and 5.5/6/7 ps/mm. Layer-specific impedances and via discontinuities are not extracted.
Reference case has an ideal common ground and supply. Additional 1/3 nH series loop inductance is a separate sensitivity, not a measurement or a solved actual return path.
ODT model is fixed in its non-driving input state through each run; no timing of mode-register writes, ODT enable/disable or power-up is simulated.

Typical model column uses 1.35 V, 50 C; min uses 1.283 V, 110 C; max uses 1.45 V, -40 C exactly as the model labels its corners. These are model characterization conditions, not predicted temperatures or board operating approvals.
Piecewise-linear input I/V tables are preserved without fitting. Beyond the reverse-biased input-clamp table endpoint, endpoint leakage is held constant; no forward-current extrapolation is accepted.
ISSI C_comp is a die-node capacitance; C_pin is at the external ball, with series pin R/L. Package mutual coupling, package supply inductance and Rockchip package are absent.
All scalar metrics use the complete accepted SPICE samples. UI traces retain actual solver timestamps with voltage/current extrema preserved; full raw CSVs remain available.
limitations: Conditional receive-channel sensitivity only; no validation of DDR training, setup/hold, read timing, DQS, crosstalk, jitter, eye mask, BER, complete memory traffic, boot or EMC.

Model supply corner 1.45 V exceeds the earlier shared RK3566/DRAM rail maximum 1.417 V; it is retained only as an ISSI model corner, not a proposed board setting. The 110 C model corner is also not an industrial Tc operating approval.
Single DM input current is not total DRAM current, SoC current or supply current. No internal activity, refresh, regulator behavior or temperature prediction is computed.
Public exact RK3566 IBIS/IBIS-AMI/functional-power model not found in this bounded official-source search; this does not establish that Rockchip cannot provide one directly.

No selected eMMC silicon manufacturer/order code exists in the retained module description, so no unrelated memory IBIS is substituted as exact. AW-CM256SM public module data did not expose an exact executable I/O model in the bounded search. Y1 lacks an exact order code and motional parameters.

No formal vendor IBIS compliance checker or vendor reference simulator correlation was available. The adapter validates only the selected input-table/package subset with DC table fidelity, line analytic reference, KCL and timestep convergence.
Existing full-board physical-evidence score remains unchanged; this study does not turn software checks into hardware sign-off.

studies.title: TI SN74LVC1G125 manufacturer macro: camera clock and logic-domain loading
studies.summary: The unchanged TI SCEM639 macro executes, but reference output screening fails. Native U123/R125 curves are retained only as conditional model responses with declared load assumptions.

sources.title: TI SN74LVC1G125 product / exact SCEM639 behavioral model

assumptions: Source waveform has 2 ns edges and the declared amplitude/frequency; no real Y120 clock model.
10, 30 and 100 pF are load sensitivities, not extracted module/flex/probe capacitances.
Native R125 is 33 Ω; reference benches intentionally omit it. VDD is an ideal declared source.
limitations: Native PCB/schematic/BOM and frozen engine/runs are unchanged. No whole-board EM, thermal or boot solver is added.
Boundary supplies, stimulus, receiver/cable capacitance and off-state loads are declared assumptions. No PCB/package/flex transmission-line model is included.
No internal IC branch currents or temperatures are inferred. A modeled VDD-port current is a macro output, not a measured silicon current.
SCEM639 is a generic family-derived, datasheet-value macro labeled for this exact part; its typical 25 °C behavior does not establish process/temperature extremes or a qualified DPW package.
The older downloaded IBIS omits DPW package data; do not substitute another package invisibly.
No startup-through-zero qualification: VCC below 1.65 V is outside normal operation, and model formulas divide by VCC. Native OE is tied low, so real ramp behavior remains a separate requirement.
The exact macro was executed, but its undamped-reference output screening failed. Native R125 damping does not qualify that reference or cure the vendor model.

SCEM639 output LOUT is parallel to the behavioral output conductance. With a 15 pF undamped load, stored ngspice results ring beyond the declared screening envelope. Simulator cross-check or a vendor-confirmed model is required before hardware decisions.
The 120 ns reference and 400 ns native-clock experiments use fixed valid operating supplies; neither is a cold-start simulation.

sources.title: TI PCA9306 datasheet, section 8.1.7 bias-current discussion
TI support supplies LSF0102 as a PCA9306-Q1 electrical proxy

assumptions: LSF0102 KP=22 mA/V² and VTO=0.7 V are unchanged vendor proxy parameters, not exact PCA9306 electrical characteristics.
Both bus sides use assumed lumped capacitance; the ideal 10 Ω open-drain sink is a stimulus, not a SoC/sensor IO model.

Absent-low-source cases use actual total 5 µF nominal local CAM_1V8 bypass but assume 1 GΩ/1 MΩ/100 kΩ residual loads and a 1 ms external 3.3 V ramp. These are sensitivity cases, not proposed PCB changes.
limitations: Native PCB/schematic/BOM and frozen engine/runs are unchanged. No whole-board EM, thermal or boot solver is added.
Boundary supplies, stimulus, receiver/cable capacitance and off-state loads are declared assumptions. No PCB/package/flex transmission-line model is included.
No internal IC branch currents or temperatures are inferred. A modeled VDD-port current is a macro output, not a measured silicon current.
Exact PCA9306 HSPICE is encrypted and not executed; its supplied TSSOP package also differs from DQE.
The three-MOSFET proxy omits characterized package parasitics, leakage corners, temperature limits, actual external regulator and peripheral off-state loads.
No I2C firmware/address/transaction emulation, maximum-clock qualification or authoritative bleed selection is claimed.

sources.title: TI SN74LVC1G125 SCEM639 original behavioral model
TI SN74LVC1G125 SCEM579 original PSpice model

assumptions: The 1 µΩ numerical connection approximates an omitted series resistor; 15 pF is the declared external load. The v1 macro also contains 30 pF of its own output capacitance.
Supply, stimulus and temperature assumptions match across both model revisions.
limitations: Two typical reference screens do not qualify the full voltage/process/temperature/receiver-load range or DPW package.

These use 25 MHz and ideal input sources; the datasheet timing figure specifies a repetition rate up to 10 MHz and a 50 Ω generator. At 3.3 V VCC the datasheet uses 3 V input and 1.5 V crossing; these comparisons use 3.3 V input and 1.65 V crossing. Timing-range comparisons are indicative, not datasheet test reproduction.
The v1 output dependent source has no complete VDD energy accounting. No v1 supply-current or thermal prediction is published.
No v1 cold-start, OE-ramp or real camera-line study is claimed. The v2 failure remains retained.
